title: Normalize sharded-ingest sampling to restore consistent per-model Console charts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Multiple customers and internal dashboards are reporting inconsistent per-model and per-tenant breakdowns in the Redwood Console after recent ingestion changes. The symptom set: (1) short-lived spikes in a single 5m bucket that disappear after an hour, (2) per-model percentage totals not summing to account-level totals across some ranges, and (3) visual flicker when toggling date ranges in the Console's usage chart. These anomalies correlate with periods of high write throughput and with the rollout of the sharded ingestion pipeline that added probabilistic sampling at the shard frontier.
root_cause: Preliminary investigation indicates two interacting problems: 1) a shard-local sampling decision (sample rate and sampling window) was applied before deduplication and global rollup, which caused inconsistent representation when late/backfilled events arrived and were processed by a different shard; 2) the current rollup merge uses a non-deterministic tie-break on event provenance (ingestion_timestamp + shard_id) that can reorder or drop backfilled events during lookback merges, producing transient spikes and gaps in per-model charts. In short, sampling + non-deterministic merge ordering leads to non-idempotent rollups across time windows.
proposed_solution: 1) Move sampling to a deterministically keyed layer: compute sampling decisions using stable request_id + model_id hash prior to shard assignment so replays land in the same logical sample bucket. 2) Extend rollup merge to include a stable, deterministic precedence rule: prefer events by (request_id hash, original_event_time, ingestion_shard_id) and treat backfills as additive unless exact-match dedupe keys exist. 3) Add a short-term reconciliation job (windowed re-merge) for the last 7 days that re-ingests rollup materialized views using the deterministic merge logic to repair affected buckets. 4) Add end-to-end tests and synthetic workloads covering replays, late arrivals, and cross-shard reassignments.
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary): deploy deterministic sampling library to one ingestion shard ring for internal tenants and observe per-model alignment for 24h. Phase B: enable deterministic merge logic in rollup service with a readonly dry-run against production materialized views for 48h. Phase C: run reconciliation job for 7-day window once dry-run shows no divergence; monitor Console and billing dashboards. Phase D: full rollout and add synthetic playback to nightly CI to prevent regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model breakdown totals equal account-level totals for 99.99% of 5m buckets across a 72h sample after phased rollout
No new duplicated tokens or undercounts introduced in streaming/prefix telemetry (validated by token-level property checks)
Reconciliation job completes within operational window and produces a change-log of repaired buckets for audit
Dry-run merge produces zero false positives on dedupe for a 48h production sample
